title: fix(devx): let the dispatcher gate's resolver read `let`/`var`, guarded by reassignment
body:
Fixes #10918

`declaredInitializers` anchored on `const` alone, so an error code held in a `let` reduced to nothing: `resolveConstant` answered `null`, the `codehelper` branch read that as the documented runtime-value bound, and the site produced **no site and no unresolved** even when every value was a literal spelled out in the source.

The anchor now reads `const|let|var`. The mutability that admits is handled rather than ignored — a mutable binding's initializer is not the set of values it holds, so reducing it unconditionally would report a value the program may never stamp, which is the ALL-OR-NOTHING wrongness #9568 exists to refuse. Three states:

| state | answer |
| --- | --- |
| `let`/`var` never reassigned in the file | reduces exactly as the `const` spelling does — **sites** |
| `let`/`var` reassigned, initializer reduces to literals | not reduced; **reported as `unresolved`** (reason `reassigned`) |
| mutable local with no literal anywhere (`let code: unknown = null; code = read(x)`) | untouched — still the #9460 runtime-value bound, still silent |

Reassignment detection is file-local, which is complete rather than approximate: a local cannot be assigned from another file, and ES modules forbid an importer assigning to an imported binding. It is biased toward over-detection — a false positive costs a reduction (loud), a miss costs a site asserted out of a value the program may never stamp (silent).

Half 2 of the card (bare reassignment, no declarator) is deliberately **not** closed; `check:error-code-casing`'s `local-fallback` requires a declarator too, so that shape stays unowned by both gates and is recorded in the header's bounds. `#10897 is not addressed here.`

### Measured

The card's fixture table re-run at `origin/main` `a41069ba` reproduced all five rows exactly. After this change, rows 1–2 report `unresolved`; rows 3–5 (the `const` controls, including the casing-gate control) are byte-identical.

Extent of half 1, swept: **6** `let`/`var` declarations of a `code`-ish name exist under `packages/**`; **1** is stamped via `.code = <same ident>` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts:6753`, `let code: unknown | null = null`, reassigned). Its initializer is not a literal, so it falls in state 3 and reports nothing. **No `let`-held error code in the tree holds an unregistered literal** — the gap this closes is latent, not live.

Tree-wide before/after over the gate's own scan set (1913 files, 292 registered codes): sites `21 → 21`, unresolved `0 → 0`, both sets identical. No currently-reported site stops being reported.

Reverse verification: reverting the anchor alone (`(?:const|let|var)` → `const`, confirmed on disk by grep count `1 → 0` on the widened spelling and `0 → 1` on the const-only spelling) turns **13** of the new assertions red and leaves every `const`-path control green.

### Gates run locally at `6b67f12c`

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 7 families; all green, plus `check:nul-bytes`:

`check:cross-package-test-inputs` · `check:dispatcher-error-vocabulary` (self-test: *8 shapes + 143 assertions OK*; full run: *OK — 21 unregistered code-stamping site(s), all classified*) · `check:entry-guard` · `check:parse-guard` · `check:pnpm-filter-targets` · `scripts/check-ci-filter-parity.mjs` · `scripts/check-cross-package-test-inputs.mjs` · `scripts/check-nul-bytes.mjs`.
